events.content: Equinix Q3 2026 revenue total and organic revenue growth

Equinix has not yet filed or reported **Q3 2026** as of October 17, 2026: its investor-relations filing page identifies the latest quarterly filing as the **Q2 2026 Form 10-Q**, filed July 29, 2026, while Q3 earnings are scheduled for October 28, 2026. [[1, 2]] 

In the latest reported quarter, **Q2 2026 (three months ended June 30, 2026)**, Equinix generated **$2.625 billion of total revenue**, up **16% year over year** from **$2.256 billion**. [[3, 4]]

| Q2 2026 segment result | Revenue ($m) | Recurring revenue ($m) | Non-recurring revenue ($m) | Segment adjusted EBITDA ($m) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Americas | 1,251 | 1,067 | 184 | 641 |
| EMEA | 845 | 806 | 39 | 456 |
| Asia-Pacific | 529 | 504 | 25 | 299 |
| **Total** | **2,625** | **2,377** | **248** | **1,396** |

The figures above are from Equinix’s Q2 2026 Form 10-Q, which defines the company’s three reportable geographic segments as Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific and reports revenue and adjusted EBITDA by segment. [[4]] 

Americas was the largest and fastest-growing segment, with revenue up **$247 million, or 25% year over year**, to $1.251 billion; EMEA revenue rose **$78 million, or 10%**, to $845 million; and Asia-Pacific revenue rose **$44 million, or 9%**, to $529 million. [[4]] 

For context only, Equinix’s Q2 release guided to **Q3 2026 revenue of $2.525 billion to $2.575 billion**, rather than reporting a Q3 actual result. [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: Equinix Q2 2026 xScale and AI data-center leasing demand revenue figure

events.content: Equinix Q2 2026 xScale and AI data-center leasing demand revenue figure

**Q2 2026 read-through:** Equinix’s xScale leasing demand was exceptionally strong: it signed **134 MW of xScale leases across the Americas** during Q2, demonstrating substantial hyperscale capacity absorption. [[1]] 

The xScale platform had **604 MW leased** across its current portfolio at quarter-end, versus more than **2,000 MW of total capacity when fully built out**, indicating a large remaining development runway but also meaningful execution, power-availability, and preleasing requirements. [[1]] 

The Hampton transaction was included in the 134 MW and generated approximately **$120 million of non-recurring fees**, which was a material contributor to Q2’s reported **16% year-over-year revenue growth** to **$2.625 billion**. [[2]] [[3]] 

Demand was not limited to xScale: Equinix reported **23% year-over-year annualized gross-bookings growth**, its second-highest volume on record, and a record sold-but-not-yet-installed backlog. [[3]] 

Management also reported that about **30% of remaining 2026 retail expansion capacity had been pre-sold** and that more than **45% of its Q3 bookings target** had already closed, supporting a broader view of tight, accelerating demand across both retail colocation and hyperscale-oriented capacity. [[2]] 

AI is an important demand driver, but Equinix did **not** disclose what portion of the 134 MW xScale signings was specifically AI-related; its formal commentary instead characterized customer demand as broad-based across networking, cloud, and AI infrastructure. [[3]] 

The practical implication is favorable for xScale growth and monetization: Equinix is accelerating more than **7,000 cabinets** that had been scheduled for 2027 into **Q4 2026**, while lifting its full-year revenue-growth guidance to **11%–12%** from **10%–11%**. [[1]] 

Investors should normalize the quarter for the Hampton-related fee, however, because the company explicitly attributed part of Q2 revenue and profit growth to one-time xScale fees rather than recurring leasing revenue. [[3]] [[2]]

events.content: Equinix Q2 2026 AI-related data-center leasing percentage of total xScale or colocation revenue

Equinix did **not disclose a percentage of Q2 2026 leasing/bookings that was AI-related**; management characterized AI qualitatively, saying that the vast majority of its largest deals were AI-workload driven, while reporting total annualized gross bookings of **$424 million**, up 23% year over year. [[1]] [[2]] 

For xScale specifically, Equinix signed **134 MW** of leases across the Americas in Q2 2026, including the Hampton transaction; this is a megawatt leasing measure, not a stated percentage of company-wide leasing or bookings. [[3]] [[1]] 

The identifiable Q2 revenue contribution was approximately **$120 million of non-recurring xScale leasing fees** from Hampton, equivalent to **4.6% of total Q2 revenue of $2.625 billion**. [[1]] [[2]] 

On the reported revenue bridge, Equinix generated **$2.377 billion of recurring revenue (90.6% of total)** and **$248 million of non-recurring revenue (9.4%)**; the company did not publish an exact xScale/AI split of either total. [[2]] 

Thus, the defensible takeaway is: **AI was described as a major driver of large deals, xScale leasing totaled 134 MW, and the disclosed Hampton xScale fee represented roughly 4.6% of Q2 revenue—but no disclosed AI share of total leasing or revenue exists.** [[1]] [[3]] [[1]] [[2]]

Sources:

AI is an important demand driver, but Equinix did **not** disclose what portion of the 134 MW xScale signings was specifically AI-related; its formal commentary instead characterized customer demand as broad-based across networking, cloud, and AI infrastructure. [[3]] 

The practical implication is favorable for xScale growth and monetization: Equinix is accelerating more than **7,000 cabinets** that had been scheduled for 2027 into **Q4 2026**, while lifting its full-year revenue-growth guidance to **11%–12%** from **10%–11%**. [[1]] 

Investors should normalize the quarter for the Hampton-related fee, however, because the company explicitly attributed part of Q2 revenue and profit growth to one-time xScale fees rather than recurring leasing revenue. [[3]] [[2]]

The financial impact was visible in reported results: Q2 revenue was **$2.625 billion, up 16% year over year**, with the company explicitly attributing part of that growth to one-time xScale fees. [[3]] 

For capacity and capital deployment, Equinix said a significant portion of capacity planned for delivery in the remainder of 2026 had already been committed through bookings and presales, while guiding to **$5–$6 billion** of capital expenditure excluding real-estate acquisitions and xScale. [[1]]
